Google.name: Gemini 3.5 Flash
Google.description: Flagship multimodal model (May 19, 2026) now default across Gemini app, AI Mode in Search, and Gemini Enterprise. 1M context, 4x faster than other frontier models, native to Antigravity 2.0 agentic dev platform. Gemini 3.5 Pro confirmed for June 2026 GA (announced at I/O 2026, May 19): 2M-token context window, Deep Think reasoning mode, frontier multimodal; pricing expected ~$15/$60 per 1M tokens. Limited Vertex enterprise preview began in late May; Polymarket odds >70% for late-June launch. Gemini Omni 2 video editing rolled out June 16, 2026 in Pixel Drop (Android 17) — users can now chat to create and edit videos in the Gemini app, blend text/images/video, and create custom AI avatars. Lyria 3 music generation (Gemini 3 in Pixel Drop) also June 16 — text or image prompts into full tracks with custom style, vocals, and tempo on all Android 17 Pixel devices. June 17, 2026: Google Home Speaker is the first audio device built for the Gemini for Home voice assistant (pre-order $99.99, ships June 25). Gemini Live now supported on Google TV Streamer, Pixel Buds, and Pixel Watch. Pixel 10a ships with AudioLM-powered live speech-to-speech translation. AMIE research published in Nature (June 17) demonstrates primary-care-level complex disease management. Project Astra → Gemini Live improvements: continued multi-turn conversation, sub-second response, on-device visual grounding.

Amazon.name: Nova 2
Amazon.description: Amazon's Nova model family for complex reasoning, agentic workflows, and multimodal tasks. Nova 2 offers improved instruction following and lower latency via Bedrock.

OpenAI.name: GPT-5.5
OpenAI.description: Frontier reasoning model (April 23, 2026), GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.5 Pro in API (April 24). GPT-5.5 Instant default in ChatGPT since June 3, 2026. Powers Codex (including Codex Mobile preview May 14, 2026), Deep Research, voice, image, agent tools. GPT-5.6 series (Sol, Terra, Luna) GA July 9, 2026 after limited preview to trusted US partners at request of Trump administration (Office of National Cyber Director + OSTP) — OpenAI coordinated pre-deployment testing with US Center for AI Standards and Innovation and the June 2026 Executive Order on AI security. Sol ($5/$30 per 1M tokens) is the new frontier workhorse and 'strongest cybersecurity model yet', sets new SOTA on Coding Agent Index 80.0 (+2.8 over Fable 5) at less than half the output tokens in less than half the time, with 'max' and 'ultra' (multi-agent parallel workstream coordinator) settings; Terra ($2.50/$15) is balanced for everyday work; Luna ($1/$6) is fastest/most affordable. July 30, 2026 price-performance frontier push: Luna cut 80% to $0.20/$1.20 per 1M tokens, Terra cut 20% to $2/$12, Sol now ships Fast mode (replaces Priority Processing) at 2.5x speed for 2x price ($10/$60) — Luna undercuts Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite on combined I/O cost. GPT-5.6 now preferred model across Microsoft 365 Copilot (Word/Excel/PowerPoint/Cowork, July 9, 2026) and the new ChatGPT Work agent (July 9, 2026). GPT-5.5-Cyber full release June 22, 2026 as part of Daybreak. Patch the Planet (June 22, 2026) pairs Codex Security with Trail of Bits engineers.

Anthropic.name: Claude Fable 5
Anthropic.description: Anthropic's first Mythos-class generally available model (June 9, 2026) at $10/$50 per 1M tokens. SOTA on SWE-Bench Pro 80.3%, FrontierCode 29.3%, OSWorld 83.4%, Humanity's Last Exam 49.8% (57.9% w/ tools). 1M context, 128K output, adaptive thinking, vision. Falls back to Opus 4.8 for cyber/biology/chemistry/distillation. Claude Mythos 5 available to Project Glasswing (expanded June 2, 2026 from ~50 to ~150 organizations across 15+ countries including power/water/healthcare/communications and Okta, Samsung, SK Hynix, SK Telecom, NATO, ENISA). SUSPENDED June 12, 2026 by US government export control directive (Commerce Department) over alleged narrow jailbreak — disabled for all customers worldwide (including foreign national Anthropic employees) pending review; Trump administration (June 15) cited Anthropic's 'recklessness' in responding to initial concerns. Free for Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise through June 22, 2026; from June 23 requires usage credits. Claude Opus 4.8 (May 28, 2026) at $5/$25 remains the default Claude surface. Legacy claude-opus-4 and claude-sonnet-4 retired June 15, 2026. Claude Security uses Opus 4.8 (released alongside) to scan codebases and suggest patches. Claude Code v2.1.190 released June 24, 2026 contains strings foreshadowing Fable 5's return to subscriptions with weekly usage limits (superseding the pay-as-you-go credits introduced June 23); Mythos 5 cleared June 26, 2026 for ~100 pre-approved US cyber-defender organizations following two-week negotiation with Commerce Secretary Lutnick; Fable 5 still pending Pentagon/NSA sign-off.

ByteDance.name: Doubao 2.0
ByteDance.description: ByteDance multimodal model family behind Doubao experiences. Seed 2.0 Pro/Lite/Mini powers Doubao App and TRAE. Seed 2.0 Lite (April 28, 2026) is first omni-modal understanding model with cross-modal audio+video reasoning. 345M MAU as of March 2026.

Oracle.name: OCI Generative AI
Oracle.description: Oracle's fully managed generative AI service for enterprise applications with REST APIs and SDKs. Summarization, writing assistance, and chat built into Oracle Cloud.

Cohere.name: Command A+
Cohere.description: Cohere's open-source 218B-parameter MoE model (May 21, 2026) with 25B active, Apache 2.0 license. Unified across reasoning, vision, translation, and tool use. Runs on 2x H100 or a single Blackwell GPU. +20% agentic QA, +32% spreadsheet analysis vs Command A Reasoning. 85% on τ²-Bench Telecom. Powers North enterprise workspace. Companion: North Mini Code (June 15, 2026) — Cohere's first dedicated open-weight agentic coding model, 30B/3B MoE, Apache 2.0.

Moonshot.name: Kimi K3
Moonshot.description: Moonshot's 2.8-trillion-parameter open-weight flagship (July 16-17, 2026) — billed as the world's largest open-weight AI model. 1M-token context, native text + image multimodal (vision input), Kimi Delta Attention + Attention Residuals architecture with 16-of-896 expert sparse MoE (~2.5x scaling efficiency vs K2). Live on Kimi.com, Kimi Work, Kimi Code, and Kimi API; open weights ship July 27, 2026 under Modified MIT. Pricing $0.30 cached / $3.00 uncached input per 1M tokens, $15.00 output per 1M tokens. Coding/agent-first positioning — case studies include GPU kernel optimization, building a Triton-like compiler called MiniTriton from scratch, and a multi-paper astrophysics research pipeline writing 3,000+ lines of Python in ~2 hours. Moonshot acknowledges overall capability still trails Claude Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol. Internal-benchmark only until independent evals land post-July 27. K2.6 Agent Swarm (up to 300 sub-agents, 4,000 coordinated steps) and K2.7-Code (June 12, 2026, 1T/32B, $0.95/$4.00) remain available on the platform.

Baidu.name: ERNIE 5.1
Baidu.description: Baidu's flagship model (May 8, 2026) trained at 6% of comparable pre-training cost. 1,223 score on LMArena Search Arena (#4 global, #1 Chinese). Topped domestic search rankings; strong τ³-bench and SpreadsheetBench-Verified. Powers ernie.baidu.com chat and Qianfan model platform.

Google-Gemini-3.6-Flash.name: Gemini 3.6 Flash
Google-Gemini-3.6-Flash.description: Google's new workhorse Flash model (launched July 21, 2026) — successor to 3.5 Flash. 17% fewer output tokens than 3.5 Flash on the Artificial Analysis Index, up to 65% fewer on agentic benchmarks like DeepSWE by Datacurve. Knowledge cutoff advanced from January 2025 to March 2026. Priced $1.50/M input and $7.50/M output (down from $9 output on 3.5 Flash). Available in Gemini app, Gemini API (AI Studio, Android Studio), Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, and Google Antigravity. Ships with enhanced Frontier Safety safeguards for CBRN and cyber-offense domains; substantially more resistant to jailbreaks while minimizing refusals on beneficial uses.

Google-Gemini-3.5-Flash-Lite.name: Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite
Google-Gemini-3.5-Flash-Lite.description: Google's fastest, most cost-effective 3.5-class model (launched July 21, 2026). 350 output tokens/s per Artificial Analysis Index. Priced $0.30/M input, $2.50/M output. Significantly outperforms 3.1 Flash-Lite in agentic workflows across thinking levels; supports minimal/low/high thinking effort to trade latency for depth. Computer use is a built-in tool. Rolling out in Gemini app, Gemini API, Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, and Google Search.

Google-Gemini-3.5-Flash-Cyber.name: Gemini 3.5 Flash Cyber
Google-Gemini-3.5-Flash-Cyber.description: Google's cyber-security fine-tune of 3.5 Flash (announced July 21, 2026), built for finding, validating, and patching code vulnerabilities at lower per-token cost than larger models. Runs inside CodeMender, Google DeepMind's code-security agent — multiple 3.5 Flash Cyber agents combine into a single combined report; competitive performance on CyberGym benchmark. Restricted availability via limited-access pilot to governments and trusted partners to mitigate broader misuse risk.

SpaceXAI.name: Grok 4.3
SpaceXAI.description: xAI frontier model (April 17, 2026, API May 6) with 1M context, $1.25/$2.50 per 1M tokens. grok-4.20 extends to 2M context. Custom Voices TTS ($4.20/1M chars), Voice Agent API ($3/hr). grok-imagine-image-quality for image generation. Grok 5 in training on Colossus 2 (1.5GW); Polymarket now prices June 30 release at ~3-7% (down from 30s in spring). Grok V9-Medium (1.5T params, Cursor-trained coding model, built on Colossus 2) finished training May 25 with public release expected mid-June 2026 — positioned as the coding sibling of the eventual Grok 5 frontier model. June 17, 2026: Grok 4.3 GA on Amazon Bedrock via the new Mantle inference engine — #1 on Artificial Analysis Omniscience (lowest hallucination among frontier models), #1 on Tau2 Telecom (real-world tool-calling in customer-support agents), #1 on Vals AI Case Law and Corporate Finance benchmarks; configurable reasoning effort (none/low/medium/high), 1M context, OpenAI-compatible Responses API on Bedrock. Grok 4.20 (2M context) also available on Bedrock. Grok 4.5 (SpaceXAI's Opus-class model launched July 8, 2026, $2/$6 per 1M tokens — 'Opus-class model, but faster, more token-efficient and lower cost' per Elon Musk; first release since SpaceXAI public listing; trained in Memphis data centers with new datasets spanning science/engineering/math; Responses API and Chat Completions; reasoning effort Low/Medium/High; tools include function calling, web/X search, code execution) is SpaceXAI's current default and replaces prior Grok 4.3 as the workhorse for coding/app-building/office/research/writing at competitive pricing; Grok 4.3 and grok-4.20 (2M context) remain on Bedrock via the Mantle inference engine.

Anthropic-Opus-5.name: Claude Opus 5
Anthropic-Opus-5.description: Anthropic's step-change successor to Opus 4.8 (launched July 24, 2026, $5/$25 per 1M tokens, same price as Opus 4.8). 1M-context window, 128K max output, thinking on by default, full effort ladder (low/medium/high/xhigh/max). SOTA on Frontier-Bench v0.1 (more than double Opus 4.8 at lower cost per task) and within 0.5% of Fable 5's peak on CursorBench 3.2 at max effort at half the cost. 3x the next-best model on ARC-AGI 3; 1.5x the next-best on Zapier AutomationBench at the same cost. New default model on Claude Max, strongest model on Claude Pro. Also offered in Fast mode at 2x base price for ~2.5x speed. Two API betas alongside launch: mid-conversation tool changes (add/remove tools between turns without invalidating prompt cache) and server-side fallbacks that automatically route flagged requests to a recommended alternative rather than blocking. Most-aligned model in Anthropic's behavioral audit to date; lowest deceptive-behaviour rate; least susceptible to misuse. Cyber classifiers proportionally less restrictive than Fable 5's (find vulnerabilities in source code, but block binary-based scanning, pentesting, exploit generation). Available on Claude API, Bedrock, Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry. Available on Kiro for ambitious projects.

OpenAI-GPT-5.6-Sol.name: GPT-5.6 Sol
OpenAI-GPT-5.6-Sol.description: OpenAI's next-generation frontier model (GA July 9, 2026) after limited preview to trusted US partners at request of the Trump administration (Office of National Cyber Director + OSTP) — OpenAI coordinated pre-deployment testing with the US Center for AI Standards and Innovation and the June 2026 Executive Order on AI security. Sol ($5/$30 per 1M tokens) is the new frontier workhorse and OpenAI's 'strongest cybersecurity model yet' — sets new SOTA on the Coding Agent Index at 80.0 (+2.8 over Fable 5) at less than half the output tokens in less than half the time, with 'max' and 'ultra' (multi-agent parallel workstream coordinator) settings. Terra ($2.50/$15) is balanced for everyday work; Luna ($1/$6) is fastest/most affordable. GPT-5.6 Sol now preferred model across Microsoft 365 Copilot (Word/Excel/PowerPoint/Cowork, July 9, 2026) and the new ChatGPT Work agent (July 9, 2026). Powers ChatGPT Health (rolled out to all US users 18+ on web and iOS July 23, 2026, with Apple Health/Weight Watchers/MyFitnessPal/Function connectors and HealthBench Professional benchmark). Replaces GPT-5.5 as the API default behind OpenAI Presence, Codex, Deep Research, voice, image, and agent tools.

Cogent.name: Cogent VR-1
Cogent.description: Cogent Security's Mythos-class frontier reasoning model (announced July 27, 2026, San Francisco). First frontier model trained and optimized specifically for cyber defense. Given a foothold inside an enterprise, VR-1 autonomously maps the surrounding environment, connects weaknesses across cloud/identity/application/endpoint systems, and verifies proposed attack paths through execution. On the black-box configuration of IntrusionBench (released alongside the model, execution-verified benchmark for enterprise attack chains), VR-1 achieved 2x the pass@3 of the strongest frontier baseline within a 2-hour wall-clock limit / 250 agent turns. Cogent calls its validation principle 'prove, don't detonate' -- exposure gets confirmed without causing damage, persistence, or disruption. Not released openly; available only to vetted organizations through the Cogent Frontier Access Program with guardrails, policy controls, and audit logging. Pricing not publicly disclosed. Founders Vineet Edupuganti (CEO), Geng Sng (CTO), Anirudh Ravula (Head of AI).

Microsoft-MAI-Cyber-1-Flash.name: MAI-Cyber-1-Flash
Microsoft-MAI-Cyber-1-Flash.description: Microsoft AI's first in-house cybersecurity model (announced July 27, 2026) — a compact, code-heavy security model built from scratch on the MAI-Thinking-1 platform and trained on the highest-quality security data, optimized for finding and validating vulnerabilities in complex codebases. Powers MDASH, Microsoft's multi-model agentic scanning harness orchestrated by FORGE (Frontier Offensive Research & Generative Exploration, led by Georgia Tech professor Taesoo Kim). When paired with GPT-5.4 in MDASH, the combo scores 95.95-96% on CyberGym benchmark (~12 points above Mythos 5) at roughly half the cost of the prior MDASH configuration (which mixed GPT-5.4, 5.4 mini, and 5.3 Codex). Available in preview via Microsoft Defender / Microsoft Security Exposure Management starting November 3, 2026 — same window as Project Perception.

Google-Gemini-Robotics-2.name: Gemini Robotics 2
Google-Gemini-Robotics-2.description: Google DeepMind's most advanced vision-language-action (VLA) model for embodied AI (launched July 30, 2026). Converts vision and language input into motor control for full humanoids (feet to fingertips) and other bi-arm robots; new level of dexterous manipulation on hands and grippers. Paired with Gemini Robotics ER 2 (reasoning/planning) and Gemini Robotics On-Device 2 (efficiency). VLA and On-Device models available to early-access partners; ER 2 publicly available via Gemini API, Google AI Studio, and in private preview on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform.

Google-Gemini-Robotics-ER-2.name: Gemini Robotics ER 2
Google-Gemini-Robotics-ER-2.description: Google DeepMind's most capable embodied reasoning (ER) model (launched July 30, 2026) — a vision-language model acting as the high-level brain for robots. Chats with humans, understands the physical world, plans multi-step tasks lasting several minutes, hands off motor execution to lower-level VLA models (e.g., Gemini Robotics 2), natively calls tools like Google Search, and introduces multi-robot collaboration so robot teams can work together in shared spaces. Publicly available to developers via Gemini API, Google AI Studio, and in private preview on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform.

Microsoft-Copilot-Super-App.name: Microsoft Copilot Super App
Microsoft-Copilot-Super-App.description: Microsoft's unified Copilot surface confirmed by CEO Satya Nadella on the July 29, 2026 earnings call — ships this quarter. Merges Copilot chat, GitHub Copilot coding, Copilot Cowork, and long-running Autopilots (including the always-on Microsoft Scout) into a single super app spanning both consumer and commercial experiences. Backed by multi-model architecture (GPT-5.6, Claude, MAI-Thinking-1, MAI-Image/Voice, others) with movement between models per task. Wired into Agent 365 governance, IT Ops, SecOps, FinOps, and CRM/ERP skills. Shift from per-seat to per-seat-plus-consumption pricing already underway across Cowork and Agent 365. Microsoft posted $90B in quarterly revenue; Copilot paid seats now surpass 30M.

Meta.name: Muse Spark
Meta.description: Meta's latest flagship model (April 8, 2026), ranks 4th on AI Index with strong health and science reasoning. Multimodal with tool-use and Contemplating mode for multi-agent reasoning. Muse Spark 1.1 (launched July 9, 2026 by Meta Superintelligence Labs) is a major upgrade focused on agentic tasks — major gains in tool use, computer use, coding, and multimodal understanding. Performs well on popular agentic setups (planning mode, goal conditioning, subagent delegation, context compaction); 'Thinking' mode available now in the Meta AI app and on meta.ai. First release of the new Meta Model API (public preview) — developers can begin building with Muse Spark 1.1, paired with long-context handling.

DeepSeek.name: DeepSeek V4
DeepSeek.description: Open-model MoE family (V4-Pro: 1.6T total / 49B active, V4-Flash: 284B / 13B active, April 24, 2026 preview; graduated to GA on July 24, 2026 alongside peak/off-peak pricing). 1M context, Apache 2.0 licensed. 27% of per-token inference FLOPs vs V3. V4-Pro: $0.435/$0.87, V4-Flash: $0.14/$0.28 per 1M tokens (cache hit from $0.0028/$0.003625); 2× multiplier during Beijing peak windows (09:00–12:00 and 14:00–18:00 local time) since the July 24 GA. Legacy deepseek-chat/deepseek-reasoner retired 2026-07-24 15:59 UTC; all API traffic must now use deepseek-v4-pro / deepseek-v4-flash identifiers with the thinking parameter for reasoning mode.

Mistral.name: Medium 3.5
Mistral.description: Mistral's unified 128B dense model (April 28, 2026) replaces Medium 3.1, Magistral, and Devstral 2. 256K context, 77.6% SWE-Bench Verified, open weights under Modified MIT. Default in Le Chat and Vibe CLI (May 5, 2026).

Alibaba.name: Qwen 3.8-Max
Alibaba.description: Alibaba's 2.4-trillion-parameter flagship preview launched at the World AI Conference in Shanghai (July 19, 2026) — first Qwen above 1T to natively process images, video, and documents alongside text. Alibaba's official pitch: 'second only to Fable 5.' Currently live as Qwen3.8-Max-Preview on Alibaba Cloud Token Plan (Lite $6/2,500 credits/week → Pro $68/40,000 credits/week), Qoder coding platform, and QoderWork productivity suite at 10% of standard rate; full open-weight release promised 'soon' (no date/license/Hugging Face repo yet). No independent benchmarks published — Alibaba acknowledges model behavior may change during preview and that they have not disclosed active-parameter count or MoE-vs-dense architecture. Predecessor Qwen 3.7-Max (May 26, 2026, 1T+ parameters, 1M context, 35-hour autonomous runs, top-tier on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index) powers the Wukong enterprise platform, Qwen App with full Taobao integration, and Qwen Cloud agentic platform. Qwen3.7-Plus (June 2, 2026, multimodal agent model, ~$0.40/$2.40 per 1M tokens, #5 globally on Vision Arena, ScreenSpot Pro 79.0 / Terminal-Bench 70.3) remains available. Model Studio CLI (June 8, 2026) open-sources 150+ multimodal models (Qwen, HappyHorse, Wan, DeepSeek, Kimi). Qwen-Robot Suite launched June 17, 2026 — Qwen-RobotManip, Qwen-RobotNav, Qwen-RobotWorld for manipulation/navigation/world-model robotics.

Microsoft.name: MAI-Thinking-1
Microsoft.description: Microsoft AI's first in-house reasoning model (June 2, 2026, Build) with 35B active / ~1T total MoE params, 256K context, no third-party distillation. Matches Sonnet 4.6 in blind side-by-side, competitive with Opus 4.6 on SWE-Bench Pro coding. In private preview on Microsoft Foundry, will move to MAI Playground public preview. Also available on Fireworks AI, Baseten, Open Router.

Google.name: Gemma 4
Google.description: Google's open model family (April 2, 2026) for lightweight multimodal deployment. Gemma 4 Assistant enables speculative decoding for Gemma 4 models. Apache 2.0 license.

MiniMax.name: MiniMax M3
MiniMax.description: MiniMax's flagship open-weight model (May 31, 2026) with 1M-token context, native multimodality (image+video input, desktop computer use), and frontier coding/agentic performance. 59.0% SWE-Bench Pro, 83.5 BrowseComp, 70.06% OSWorld-Verified. Powered by MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA) — 9x prefill, 15x decode speedup at 1M context, 1/20th per-token compute. Token Plan $20/$50/$120/mo. Open weights shipping within 10 days of release.

Nous Research.name: Hermes 3
Nous Research.description: Nous Research's open-weight instruction-tuned model series, evolving into the Hermes Agent (189K GitHub stars, MIT, v0.16.0 'The Surface Release' June 6, 2026). 40+ tools, MCP integration, persistent memory, scheduled tasks, messaging gateway across Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp/Signal. Optimized for local agentic workflows on NVIDIA RTX PCs and DGX Spark with Qwen 3.6, Llama, Mistral via Ollama or LM Studio.

NVIDIA.name: Nemotron 3 Ultra
NVIDIA.description: NVIDIA's 550B total / 55B active LatentMoE (Mamba-2 + MoE + Attention hybrid) with Multi-Token Prediction, released June 4, 2026 under OpenMDW-1.1. 1M context, NVFP4 quantization runs on Hopper/Blackwell/Ampere, 5x faster inference vs other open models, 30% lower cost to task completion on Terminal Bench 2. 20T pretraining tokens. Packaged as NIM microservice with OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible APIs. Companion: Nemotron 3 Embed (released July 16, 2026) — open + commercially-available embedding family with 8B flagship ranking #1 on RTEB (78.5% NDCG@10) and 75.5% on MMTEB Retrieval, plus 1B BF16 and 1B NVFP4 Blackwell-optimized variants; 32k context, multilingual + code retrieval, day-0 on Hugging Face and as an NVIDIA NIM microservice; supported on vLLM, OpenRouter, and AI Cloud inference partners (Baseten, Bitdeer AI, DeepInfra, Friendli AI). Adopted by Automation Anywhere, Palantir, Zep, Zoom for agentic retrieval / agent memory / code retrieval / enterprise search.

Z.ai.name: GLM 5.2
Z.ai.description: Z.ai's flagship open-weight model (announced June 13, 2026 on Coding Plan; full launch June 16, 2026, the day after Fable 5 was suspended). 744B total / ~40B active MoE (384 experts), 1M-token solid lossless context, 128K max output, 28.5T pretraining tokens. New IndexShare architecture reuses the indexer across every 4 sparse-attention layers — 2.9x per-token FLOPs reduction at 1M context; improved MTP layer for speculative decoding boosts acceptance length up to 20%. Strongest open-source long-horizon coding agent: trails Opus 4.8 by 1% on FrontierSWE, beats GPT-5.5 and Opus 4.7 on multiple agentic benchmarks, highest-ranked open model on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (81.0 vs Opus 85.0) and SWE-bench Pro (62.1). Beats GLM-5.1 by +19 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and +3.7 on SWE-bench Pro. Pure MIT license — no regional limits, positioned by Z.ai as 'frontier intelligence belongs to everyone.' First shipped to GLM Coding Plan subscribers (June 13); full open-weight release on Hugging Face under zai-org (mid-June 2026). Z.ai (formerly Zhipu AI, HKEX:02513, IPO January 2026, +820% since listing) positions GLM-5.2 as the open-model beneficiary of Anthropic's Fable 5 export suspension.

Cohere.name: North Mini Code
Cohere.description: Cohere's first open-weight agentic coding model (June 15, 2026, Apache 2.0 from launch). 30B-parameter MoE with 3B active parameters, designed for multi-step tool-using work in agents like Claude Code and Cursor. Companion to the closed-weight Command A+ enterprise family. Frames the developer-tooling sovereignty gap the same way Cohere framed enterprise AI sovereignty — who controls the coding agent controls how engineering evolves.

ThinkingMachines.name: Inkling
ThinkingMachines.description: Thinking Machines Lab's first open-weight multimodal MoE (launched July 15, 2026, by Mira Murati's team). 975B total / 41B active, 1M-token context, pretrained on 45T tokens of text + images + audio + video, natively multimodal. Day-0 weights on Hugging Face in BF16 and NVFP4 (Blackwell-optimized) checkpoints with speculative MTP layers; day-0 support in transformers, SGLang, vLLM, llama.cpp. First model trained end-to-end on NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems via the Tinker customization partnership. Thinking Machines explicitly states Inkling is 'not the strongest overall model available today, open or closed' — positioned as a broad, balanced base for fine-tuning on Tinker (their customization platform) rather than a leaderboard topper. Available at 50% launch discount on Tinker (64K and 256K context); Inkling-Small (276B total / 12B active) previewing now, weights pending. Bridgewater Associates and others already cite strong fine-tuning results. Deployed via TogetherAI, Fireworks, Modal, Databricks, Baseten. Companion: Inkling Playground in Tinker console with agentic web search.

Mind Lab.name: Macaron-V1
Mind Lab.description: Mind Lab's first official agent model release (July 21, 2026) — open-weight flagship with Mixture-of-LoRA (MoL) architecture, separate LoRA specialists for agent, coding, chat, and Generative UI tasks. Two variants: Macaron-V1-Venti (748B parameters, 744B base GLM-5.2 + four 1B LoRA specialists; first model post-trained from GLM-5.2) and Macaron-V1-Tall (50B parameters, 35B Qwen 3.6 base + four 3.7B LoRA specialists, designed for local deployment). LongStraw enables training at context lengths up to 2M tokens; MindForge/MinT agentic RL infrastructure trained on production Pi and Claude Code harness. Evaluated on VitaBench, PinchBench, SWE-Verified, DeepSWE, SWE Atlas QnA, TerminalBench 2.1, UI4A-Bench — Venti matches or outperforms Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5, and Gemini 3.1 Pro across most tracks while remaining open and self-hostable. Coding is the closest-to-frontier track, not ahead. UI4A is Macaron's code-native Generative UI solution. Open weights on Hugging Face (macaron-v1-venti, macaron-v1-coding-venti, macaron-v1-tall); hosted API at mint.macaron.im (overseas) and mintcn.macaron.xin (China). Macaron Artifacts Claude Code plugin visualizes UI4A output.

AntLing.name: Ling-3.0-flash
AntLing.description: Ant Group's InclusionAI released Ling-3.0-flash on July 23, 2026 — a hybrid-reasoning MoE built for production-scale agent inference. 124B total / ~5.1B active parameters per token (roughly 1/8 total and 1/12 active vs the 1T-parameter Ring-2.6-1T flagship). Native hybrid-linear attention stack interleaveing KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) and MLA layers in a 5:1 ratio, with ~1/64 expert activation. 256K-token native context window extendable up to 1M; dual thinking/non-thinking modes. Targets coding agents, search/research agents, and enterprise knowledge workflows — InclusionAI claims it 'matches or beats' their 1T flagship on most benchmarks shown (MCP-Atlas, SkillsBench, WideSearch, BrowseComp, Tau3-banking, SysBench) but no public numeric benchmark table, technical report, or model card at launch. Free through August 3, 2026 on Novita, Vercel AI Gateway (inclusionai/ling-3.0-flash-free), ZenMux, and OpenRouter (inclusionai/ling-3.0-flash:free); standard pricing TBD. Predecessor Ling-1T, Ling-2.6-flash, and Ling-flash-2.0 all shipped MIT — license for Ling-3.0-flash not yet confirmed at launch.

FLUX-3.name: FLUX 3
FLUX-3.description: Black Forest Labs' new multimodal frontier model (announced July 23, 2026, bfl.ai/blog/flux-3) — jointly trained on images, video, and audio within a unified flow-matching architecture, extended to predict robotic actions. Up to 20-second video clips with native synchronized audio in a single generation; FLUX 3 Video and FLUX 3 Action (FLUX-mimic robotics) are in gated Early Access via API and private weights; FLUX 3 Image expected in the coming weeks; FLUX 3 Dev (open-weight multimodal backbone covering video/audio/image + action prediction) planned for later in 2026. Tested by Canva, Burda, Magnific, Krea, Picsart. BFL's first public video generation model and a step beyond image-only FLUX Dev releases. Gated Early Access pricing not yet announced.

Google.name: Gemini Spark
Google.description: 24/7 personal AI agent powered by Gemini 3.5 Flash (May 19, 2026). Now with Notebooks for project organization, sync with NotebookLM. Deep Think and Deep Research Max modes available. Project Mariner capabilities folded into Gemini Agent. MacOS app integration announced for summer 2026. June 16, 2026 Pixel Drop / Android 17: Gemini Omni 2 video creation/editing in the Gemini app on Pixel (blend text, images, video into finished clips, build custom AI avatars); Lyria 3 music generation on all Android 17 Pixel devices (text or image prompts into tracks with custom style/vocals/tempo). June 17, 2026: Google Home Speaker ($99.99, shipping June 25, pre-orders open) is the first device built for the Gemini for Home voice assistant — natural multi-step conversations, Gemini Live ('Hey Google, let's chat'), Continued Conversation in all supported languages, 10 new voices, and Camera History Search for Nest cams. Google Home Premium ($10/mo or $100/yr) unlocks Gemini Live on the speaker, AI-powered camera history search, and Google Home Brief; free for 6 months with Home Speaker purchased before mid-September. Wear OS 7 launches same day with Personal Intelligence features (custom widgets by description, connected Google apps/chat history). Pixel 10a gains speech-to-speech translation with AudioLM. AMIE medical-AI research published in Nature (June 17, 2026) — conversational system matches primary-care physicians on complex disease management. Gemini 3.5 Flash gained native Computer Use (June 25, 2026) — 78.4 on OSWorld, ahead of Gemini 3 Flash (65.1) and GPT-5.4 mini (72.1); trails GPT-5.5 (78.7) and Opus 4.8 (83.4). Available via Gemini API and Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform with prompt-injection safeguards. Gemini 3.5 Pro GA pushed from June to July 2026 (June 23 announcement) to incorporate early-tester feedback — 2M-token context and Deep Think reasoning mode still planned. Google DeepMind + A24 research partnership announced June 22, 2026 for creator-facing AI tooling. July 1, 2026: Gemini Spark macOS beta launched for Google AI Ultra subscribers in the US — Spark added to the existing Gemini desktop app, can work with files on the computer, sort/organize files, use files as source for new Google Workspace docs/spreadsheets, and will soon handle remote tasks from phones. Added Google Tasks and Google Keep support (a long-requested gap). Now integrates with Canva, Dropbox, Instacart, OpenTable, Zillow Rentals. Real-time topic tracking for sports/stocks/news/social media/blogs/shopping/weather. Custom MCP support rolling out — users can connect their favorite apps to build a tailored assistant.

OpenAI.name: Presence
OpenAI.description: Enterprise platform announced July 22, 2026 for deploying trusted voice and chat agents across customer and internal workflows. Combines model reasoning with policies, guardrails, permissions, evaluations, and human escalation; limited general availability with OpenAI deployment support.

Microsoft.name: Copilot
Microsoft.description: Powered by GPT-5.5 Instant (May 7, 2026) across web, work, and Microsoft 365 surfaces. Agent Platform, Agents SDK, and Copilot Studio for enterprise orchestration. MAI-Thinking-1 (June 2, 2026) available in private preview for in-house reasoning. Opus 4.8 and Fable 5 in GitHub Copilot. Microsoft Scout (June 2, 2026, Frontier preview) is the first Autopilot — always-on personal agent integrated into Teams/Outlook/OneDrive, built on OpenClaw. New Copilot superapp launch. June 16, 2026: Copilot Cowork GA worldwide with usage-based pricing (1 cent per Copilot Credit, or P3 tier with volume discount) on top of the M365 Copilot license ($30/mo enterprise / $20/mo Business). Cowork runs in Microsoft's cloud, not on user devices — acts on docs inside the customer's M365 tenant. Admins can enable Cowork, set per-tenant/group/user spending limits, and receive spend alerts. Model options in Cowork: Anthropic Opus 4.8, Sonnet 4.6, Frontier program users get GPT-5.5 plus Microsoft's own Cowork 1 model; Microsoft reportedly planning a hosted DeepSeek option to lower costs. June 16: Microsoft IQ generally available across GitHub Copilot, Foundry, Copilot Studio (Work IQ GA APIs for agents) — new context layer grounds agents in world knowledge + enterprise knowledge; Agent 365 control plane for observing/governing/managing/securing agents. GitHub Copilot app in technical preview (June 8) for desktop agent-native workflows.

Meta.name: Meta AI
Meta.description: Powered by Muse Spark. Meta AI app rebuilt natively on May 12, 2026: Contemplating mode (multi-agent visible parallel reasoning), Live AI camera for real-time vision streaming, Marketplace shopping agent across WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook. Free at meta.ai and across Meta apps, Instagram, Facebook, Messenger, WhatsApp. Rolling out to Ray-Ban Meta glasses. Meta Business Agent (June 3, 2026) is the customer-facing business AI deployed on WhatsApp, Messenger, and Instagram (1M+ businesses, 1B+ daily threads) with morning briefings. Meta Business Agent Platform provides enterprise-scale agent building, customization, and deployment with Shopify/Zendesk/Shopee connectors. Meta Creator Assistant (June 14, 2026) is the conversational AI inside Facebook creator dashboards that explains audience data, content performance, and engagement patterns in plain language (US, Canada, India). Meta One Plus ($7.99) and Meta One Premium ($19.99) AI plans launched May 27, 2026 in Singapore, Guatemala, Bolivia. Facebook AI Mode launched June 15, 2026 — new search tab on Facebook that uses Meta AI to surface conversational answers pulled from public posts across Groups, Reels, and Marketplace (US first). Meta Edits App desktop version and AI Production Assistant launched June 15, 2026 at LA creator event — desktop video editor with AI assistant for content ideas and analytics-based guidance, integrates with Adobe Premiere / DaVinci Resolve workflows. Meta swapped its content moderation and support stack to Muse Spark (June 25, 2026) — Meta Superintelligence Labs reports 13% fewer errors than human reviewers and 10% more actual violations caught versus the prior Google Gemini pipeline; pushing past 90% LLM moderation for some content types by year-end 2026. Meta Glasses launched June 23, 2026 in partnership with EssilorLuxottica — 26 styles, prescription-lens compatible, $299+ — first AI glasses to ship with Meta AI powered by Muse Spark from day one (also now rolling out to Ray-Ban Meta and Oakley Meta glasses in US/Canada). July 24, 2026: Meta AI upgraded to a proactive task-completion agent powered by Muse Spark 1.1 — plans multi-step projects (home renovation with Marketplace integration, half-marathon training plans with calendar sync), runs daily briefings, does meal planning and product-launch alerts, creates presentations from web research (synthesizes academic papers and creator posts into editable slides), and edits outputs in real time. Rolling out first in select markets via the Meta AI app and meta.ai, with WhatsApp and additional countries to follow. Meta frames it as 'personal superintelligence' — moves beyond Q&A into autonomous execution across connected apps.

Amazon.name: Amazon Q
Amazon.description: Enterprise-first assistant grounded in AWS services and company data. Two tiers: Q Business for knowledge work, Q Developer for coding. Alexa for Shopping (May 13, 2026) replaces Rufus, integrates shopping capabilities into main Alexa experience.

DeepSeek.name: DeepSeek Chat
DeepSeek.description: Powered by DeepSeek V4 with multimodal image recognition (April 29, 2026). Expert Mode (Pro) and Instant Mode (Flash) available. Optimized for Claude Code and OpenClaw. Legacy deepseek-chat/deepseek-reasoner retire Jul 24, 2026. Native image understanding launched June 18, 2026 (DeepSeek AI Assistant v2.1.8) — describe/interpret/answer questions about images directly in chat, available to free and paid users. Recognizes objects, landmarks, can solve math problems from images; person identification remains inconsistent.

Mistral.name: Vibe
Mistral.description: Mistral's unified AI agent (rebranded from Le Chat, May 28, 2026) with Work Mode (long-running multi-step tasks with parallel tool calls, recurring scheduled jobs, 100+ connectors, MCP) and Code Mode (remote cloud coding sessions in isolated sandboxes, GitHub PR integration, Slack trigger). New VS Code extension and JetBrains/Zed ACP integration. Powered by Mistral Medium 3.5. Pro $14.99/mo, Team $24.99/user/mo. 20+ MCP-powered connectors added June 18, 2026 (Databricks, Snowflake, GitHub, Stripe, Asana) with one-click memory import from ChatGPT; available on free plan. Vibe (formerly Le Chat) consolidates Work Mode, Code Mode, and Chat Mode.

ByteDance.name: Doubao
ByteDance.description: Powered by Doubao 2.0 and Seed 2.0. 345M MAU (March 2026). Paid subscriptions launched May 4: Standard 68 yuan, Advanced 200 yuan, Professional 500 yuan.

Tencent.name: Yuanbao
Tencent.description: Powered by Hunyuan 3.0 (Hy3) MoE, 295B total params, 21B active, 256K context — fast-and-slow thinking fused. 9 legacy models (HY 2.0 Think, hunyuan-T1-latest, hunyuan-turbos, hunyuan-standard, hunyuan-role, etc.) retire June 26, 2026; multimodal vision models (HY Vision 1.5 Instruct, hunyuan-turbos-vision, hunyuan-t1-vision, hunyuan-turbos-vision-video) retire June 22, 2026. New multimodal lineup: HY-Vision-2.0-Instruct, HY-Vision-1.5-Thinking, HY-Vision-Video, YT-VITA on TokenHub. HunyuanVideo-Avatar open-sourced for voice-driven digital humans (May 28, 2026). API on TokenHub at $0.18/M input, $0.59/M output.

Alibaba.name: Qwen Chat
Alibaba.description: Powered by Qwen 3.7-Max (May 26, 2026) with 35-hour autonomous runs, multilingual chat, agentic coding, and advanced reasoning. Full Taobao integration (4B+ products) for agentic shopping. Shopping assistant with AI try-on. Compatible with Qoder coding platform.

HuggingFace.name: HuggingChat
HuggingFace.description: Multi-model open chat surface for Llama, Qwen, Mistral, and more. Inference API 3.0 with edge deployment, 10x latency improvements, offline inference.

Perplexity.name: Perplexity
Perplexity.description: Answer engine with GPT-5.5 orchestration. Personal Computer for Mac (May 11). Computer Agent with Workflows, Teams integration, Snowflake/Databricks connectors. Computer in Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook (May 28, 2026); Teams integration from earlier in May. Harvard Business School study (June 10, 2026): Computer cuts estimated task time by 87% and cost by 94% across 10,000 matched pairs. Personal Computer with local inference (hybrid local-server orchestrator) coming in July 2026 — first product to treat compute as one more thing to orchestrate across machine and cloud. Brain (June 18, 2026, Research Preview, Max + Enterprise Max) — self-improving work-memory system that builds a context graph of Computer sessions, teaches itself overnight how to do recurring work better, shows its sources, and improves answer correctness +25% / recall +16% / cost -13% on repeated tasks.

MiniMax.name: MiniMax Agent
MiniMax.description: MiniMax's AI assistant powered by MiniMax M3 (June 1, 2026) with Agent Team building, MSA-powered 1M-context reasoning, habit learning, and all-in-one chat with skills, memories, and schedules. Desktop app available. Token Plan tiers $20/$50/$120/mo.

Cohere.name: Coral
Cohere.description: Cohere's enterprise chat assistant (May 2026) powered by Command A+. North workspace integration for grounded answers over enterprise data. Multi-session memory and agentic tool use. Free and Pro tiers.

Moonshot.name: Kimi
Moonshot.description: Moonshot's flagship AI assistant (May 2026) powered by Kimi K2.6 with K2.6 Agent Swarm (up to 300 sub-agents, 4,000 coordinated steps) and Kimi Claw cloud teammate. Long-context chat, web search, multimodal inputs, deep research, agent swarm workflows. Kimi Work (June 8/12 2026) is the local-first desktop variant — see Sovereign Agent. Free, Moderato $19/mo, Allegretto $39/mo, Allegro $99/mo.

Apple.name: Siri AI
Apple.description: Apple's Siri AI assistant, unveiled at WWDC26 (June 1, 2026) as an entirely new version of Siri powered by next-generation Apple Foundation Models. Profoundly more capable and conversational, with personal context understanding, onscreen awareness, broad world knowledge, Visual Intelligence, and a dedicated Siri app to revisit conversations (iCloud-synced). New architecture routes between on-device models and Private Cloud Compute; the Foundation Models framework gives any app direct access to the on-device models powering Apple Intelligence. iOS 27 / iPadOS 27 / macOS 27 / watchOS 27 / visionOS 27 / tvOS 27; available for developer testing today, beta later this year, English first, free software update this fall. Supported on iPhone 16+ and 15 Pro/Pro Max, iPad mini (A17 Pro) and M1+ iPads, MacBook Neo (A18 Pro) and M1+ Macs, Apple Vision Pro, Apple Watch Series 9+/Ultra 2+/SE 3 (paired with AI-enabled iPhone). The Image Playground API also gains a powerful new generative model on Private Cloud Compute with photorealistic output and refinement via natural language.

Claude Tag.name: Claude Tag (Slack)
Claude Tag.description: Anthropic's persistent, channel-scoped Claude teammate for Slack (launched June 23, 2026 in beta for Claude Enterprise / Team, replacing the Claude in Slack app — migration deadline August 3, 2026). Single @Claude identity per org; admins scope channels, tools, data sources, and codebases. Optional ambient mode for proactive follow-ups, scheduled tasks, and cross-channel context. Breaks work into stages and posts updates in the Slack thread; employees can hand off half-finished tasks between team members. Anthropic reports Claude Tag wrote/merged 65% of the company's own product-team code internally — now available externally as a separate enterprise SKU, framed as 'the beginning of an evolution of Claude Code.' Powered by Claude Opus 4.8.

Anthropic-Sonnet-5.name: Claude Sonnet 5
Anthropic-Sonnet-5.description: Anthropic's most agentic Sonnet model (June 30, 2026). Introductory pricing $2/$10 per 1M tokens through August 31, 2026, then $3/$15 standard. Available on Claude Platform, AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Foundry.

Anthropic-Reflect.name: Claude Reflect
Anthropic-Reflect.description: Anthropic's built-in usage dashboard for Claude (launched July 9, 2026 in beta for Free, Pro, and Max users with memory turned on). Tracks and visualizes how you use Claude and your broader AI habits — topic summaries, usage patterns, types of tasks you run. Surfaces suggestions (e.g., 'use Projects to avoid re-explaining context across repeated tasks') and tools to set quiet hours or schedule breaks. Frames AI as a productivity partner in your daily workflow rather than a chat destination. Expandable later to include a view of time spent using Claude.

SpaceXAI.name: Grok
SpaceXAI.description: Powered by Grok 4.3 with Connectors for web, iOS, Android. MCP server support. Custom Voices (Apr 30, 2026), $4.20 per 1M characters for TTS. Grok Skills (May 22, 2026) for persistent custom expertise, file/deck/spreadsheet/PDF generation. Grok Build early beta for SuperGrok Heavy subscribers (May 14, 2026). Grok Business and Enterprise tiers. Grok Build Plugin Marketplace (June 11, 2026) with skills/MCP/plugins from MongoDB, Vercel, Sentry, Chrome DevTools, Cloudflare, Superpowers. Gopuff Go agent (June 9, 2026) powered by Grok text/audio/image. eToro Tori (June 10, 2026) with real-time market sentiment from X. Grok Voice API default for Vapi (June 3, 2026). June 15, 2026: Grok Build gains multi-session manager — manage many coding sessions at once, see what each is doing, reply to ones that need you, and dispatch new work. Grok V9-Medium (1.5T params, Cursor-trained coding model) finished training May 25 with public release expected mid-June 2026 (Polymarket ~30% odds of Grok 5 by June 30, 2026; Grok 5 still training on Colossus 2 1.5GW). June 16, 2026: Grok for PowerPoint launched — generate full slide decks directly in PowerPoint from a Grok prompt. June 17, 2026: Grok 4.3 GA on Amazon Bedrock — see Foundation Models entry for benchmarks and pricing. Agent Dashboard in Grok Build (June 15) gives a unified view of running agents across cloud/local. Grok for Word add-in launched June 18, 2026 — free Microsoft 365 add-in turns notes into structured documents, fixes grammar, brings research from web/X/connectors (SharePoint, Google Drive) directly into Word. Also available for PowerPoint and Excel. Grok Build /goal command launched June 22, 2026 — long-running autonomous tasks with sub-agents implementing and verifying a single user-defined goal (significant repositioning of Grok Build as a multi-step agent platform). Firecrawl plugin (June 23, 2026) and MongoDB plugin (June 24, 2026) added to the Grok Build Plugin Marketplace. Grok + Interactive Brokers integration launched June 22, 2026 — query portfolio data, research investments, analyze positions using AI; trade execution requires explicit user approval.

OpenAI-Health.name: ChatGPT Health
OpenAI-Health.description: OpenAI's dedicated health experience (rolled out to all logged-in US users 18+ on web and iOS on July 23, 2026, on Free, Go, Plus, and Pro plans). Built on GPT-5.6 Sol, OpenAI's strongest model for health per OpenAI; comes with the open HealthBench Professional benchmark for clinical chat evaluation. Securely connects Apple Health, Weight Watchers, MyFitnessPal, and Function, plus post-visit notes, care-team notes, lab results, and medications with end-to-end encryption. Day-one ChatGPT will ask permission before using connected health context to personalize responses; Health tab data receives additional encryption protection. Powering ChatGPT for Clinicians (free for verified US physicians, NPs, PAs, pharmacists) and OpenAI for Healthcare specialized tools. OpenAI's terms still disclaim diagnostic/therapeutic use; reinforces that Health 'supports, not replaces, professional care.' Follows the same model in ChatGPT Health tab launch (January 2026) and GPT-5.6 Sol 'strongest model for health' claim (June 2026).

Anthropic-Economic-Index.name: Anthropic Economic Index Connector
Anthropic-Economic-Index.description: Anthropic's Claude connector for the Anthropic Economic Index (launched July 22, 2026) — gives anyone with claude.ai a chat interface to real datasets on how AI is being used across the economy. Enable from the Connectors menu in about a minute; works in any conversation with any Claude model. Asks questions like 'Which occupations use AI the most?' or 'How have automation patterns changed year over year?' and Claude answers from the underlying Index tables with links back to the source data. Exposes the Index as a tool that Claude queries programmatically, then returns a cited answer with the relevant slice. Doubles as a live example of MCP-style data connectors inside Claude for anyone building similar tools for their own datasets. The underlying datasets remain freely downloadable on Anthropic's website for users who want to run their own analysis.

SpaceXAI-Workflows.name: Grok Build Workflows
SpaceXAI-Workflows.description: SpaceXAI's multi-agent orchestration primitive in Grok Build (launched July 23, 2026) — write and run workflows that fan a complex task out across hundreds of parallel agents and verify the results before reporting back. Authored by Grok from a plain-language description (no script writing required); smoke-checked before launch; auto-improved between runs. Budget per run is 128 agents (up to 1,024 for big jobs). Progress is saved as the run goes, so pause/resume never redoes finished work. Saved workflows live in `.grok/workflows/` (team-shared) or `~/.grok/workflows/` (per-user) and each becomes its own slash command taking arguments. Built-in `/deep-research` ships with the release: parallel investigators, verify every claim against sources, return a cited report. Use cases include reviewing every feature in a large PR, triaging the last 100 Linear issues into a top-10 action list, and auditing every route handler for missing auth checks with independent skeptic verification.

Anthropic.name: Claude
Anthropic.description: Default on Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.8 for max capability. Claude Fable 5 (Mythos-class) SUSPENDED June 12–June 30, 2026 by US export control directive — REDEPLOYED July 1, 2026 after US export controls lifted (new safety classifier blocks the Amazon-reported technique in 99%+ cases). Free for Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise through June 22, then metered credits from June 23. Claude for Small Business (May 13) with Quickbooks, PayPal, HubSpot, Canva, Docusign connectors. Claude Cowork GA (April 9) on macOS/Windows. Microsoft 365 add-ins for Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Outlook. Effort control across all plans. Anthropic-DXC alliance (June 11, 2026) and TCS partnership (June 12, 2026) for regulated industries. June 15, 2026: Agent SDK / claude -p / GitHub Actions usage moves from subscription limits to a separate monthly credit ($20 Pro, $100 Max 5x, $200 Max 20x, one-time claim, no rollover); legacy claude-opus-4 and claude-sonnet-4 retire. June 16, 2026: Multilingual voice mode upgrade rolling out across iOS/Android with 18 new languages (German, Portuguese, Chinese, Japanese, Russian, Ukrainian, more), real-time mid-conversation language switching, push-to-talk, and redesigned phone-call icon. Workspace agents (April 22) available in research preview in ChatGPT Business/Enterprise/Edu/Teachers plans with credit-based pricing from May 6, 2026. June 17, 2026: Seoul office opens under KiYoung Choi; MOU with Korea's Ministry of Science and ICT on AI safety and cybersecurity, evaluating model safety in Korean with the Korea AI Safety Institute. Claude Design major overhaul (June 17) — design system imports from GitHub repos, design files, or raw uploads; new admin role can approve a system and lock edits; /design-sync command in Claude Code imports the local codebase's design system into Claude Design; /design command in Claude Code creates/edits/syncs design projects without leaving the terminal; bidirectional Claude Design ↔ Claude Code hand-off; token-efficient. Claude Opus 5 (launched July 24, 2026, $5/$25 per 1M tokens) is now the new default on Claude Max and strongest model on Claude Pro, close to Claude Fable 5 at half the price.

Anthropic-Cowork.name: Claude Cowork
Anthropic-Cowork.description: Anthropic's shared workspace for Claude (GA April 9, 2026 on macOS/Windows). Claude-controlled environment that edits files, organizes folders, and interacts with apps on Anthropic's servers — not the user's local machine. July 21, 2026: Record a Skill launched for Pro, Max, and Team — screen-record a workflow once (browser or computer use) and Claude analyzes the recording to generate a reusable, rerunnable skill. No prompt engineering required; the recording itself is the specification. Connector suggestions appear when one exists for a step in the recording. Phased rollout; early use cases include filing expenses, LinkedIn tasks, email replies, and trading alerts. Converges with ChatGPT's record-and-replay pattern (June 18, 2026) — both vendors shipping 'watch me do it once, then automate it' primitives in parallel.

Anthropic-Voice.name: Claude Voice Mode
Anthropic-Voice.description: Anthropic's voice mode for Claude (major upgrade July 23, 2026). Voice mode now runs on Claude Opus 4.8 and Sonnet 5 (not just Haiku 4.5) for the first time — users can switch models mid-conversation from the model picker; voice mode defaults to the last model used in text chat, so text and voice share conversational state. Mid-conversation tool access: Claude can invoke connected tools like Gmail, Google Calendar, Slack, Canva, and Notion during a spoken conversation with explicit per-tool permission. Language support expands from English-only to 11 languages (English, French, German, Hindi, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Brazilian Portuguese, Latin American Spanish, European Spanish) with mid-conversation language switching. Available in beta to all chat users on mobile/desktop/web; Free plan gets Claude Haiku + one connected tool; paid plans unlock Opus/Sonnet and all connected tools. Voice conversations count against regular usage limits (~20–30 voice conversations/day for free users). Same-day rival launch with OpenAI's GPT-Live desktop expansion — Anthropic's bet is depth (Opus-level reasoning + tool execution), OpenAI's is breadth (multi-agent voice orchestration across Codex and ChatGPT Work).

Google.name: Gemini Code Assist
Google.description: IDE coding agent powered by Gemini 3.5 Flash, native to Android Studio, VS Code, JetBrains. Antigravity 2.0 released May 19, 2026 as agent-first dev platform with parallel sub-agents. Gemini 3.5 Flash gained native Computer Use (June 25, 2026) — 78.4 on OSWorld, ahead of Gemini 3 Flash (65.1) and GPT-5.4 mini (72.1); trails GPT-5.5 (78.7) and Opus 4.8 (83.4). Available via Gemini API and Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform with prompt-injection safeguards. Gemini 3.5 Pro GA pushed from June to July 2026 (June 23 announcement) to incorporate early-tester feedback — 2M-token context and Deep Think reasoning mode still planned. Google DeepMind + A24 research partnership announced June 22, 2026 for creator-facing AI tooling.

OpenAI.name: Codex
OpenAI.description: IDE extension and cloud coding agent powered by GPT-5.5. Available in VS Code, GitHub, JetBrains, Xcode, Eclipse, and the Codex CLI. Mobile preview inside ChatGPT iOS/Android (May 14, 2026) supervises Codex sessions on Mac — June 8, 2026 update adds worktrees (create/switch branches and run setup scripts from device), Codex profile screen with usage stats and token activity charts, /goal support for creating/managing goals from Codex Mobile, inline review comments when viewing changed files, ask-in-thread from transcript selection, edit previously sent prompts. Safe coding commitment May 8, 2026. On AWS Bedrock (April 28, 2026). 5M+ weekly active users (June 2, 2026). Six role-specific enterprise plugins (data analytics, creative production, sales, product design, equity investing, investment banking) plus Annotations and Sites (June 2, 2026) for building/deploying internal web apps. Acquiring Ona (announced June 11, 2026) for secure customer-controlled cloud execution — Ona's persistent sandboxed environments let agents work in customer-owned clouds for hours or days. June 17, 2026: Europe/UK/Switzerland expansion brings Codex Computer Use, the Codex Chrome Extension, Memories (opt-in for EEA/UK/CH due to regional privacy rules), and Chronicle (macOS-only opt-in research preview that infers recent screen context to ground memory creation) to those regions; new Codex for Mac Dock icon options, ability to bank and save limit resets, and Computer Use support in the EU. Record & Replay plugin launched June 18, 2026 (macOS exclusive) — perform a task on your Mac once, Codex captures the workflow and packages it into a reusable skill that teams can share across the organization. Built on the plugin ecosystem that expanded to CLI/VS Code in March 2026 and added role-specific bundles in early June. Codex Remote reached GA on June 25, 2026 with QR-pairing between iOS/Android and host machines — opens phone-based control of long-running coding sessions to all paid ChatGPT subscribers (Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, Education); replaces older remote-shell approach with purpose-built relay architecture; existing connections since June 8, 2026 carry over automatically.

Anthropic.name: Claude Code
Anthropic.description: Terminal-first coding agent with IDE workflows powered by Claude Opus 4.8. Claude Fable 5 SUSPENDED June 12–June 30, 2026 by US export control directive — REDEPLOYED July 1, 2026 after US export controls lifted (new safety classifier blocks the Amazon-reported technique in 99%+ cases) — was available in GitHub Copilot, Claude API, and Claude Platform on AWS (June 9, 2026). Dynamic workflows GA in Claude Code (June 11, 2026, Code with Claude Tokyo) — Claude writes orchestration scripts running tens to hundreds of parallel subagents per session, enabled via /ultracode or asking Claude to create a workflow. Scheduled deployments and environment variable vaults in public beta in Claude Managed Agents (June 11, 2026). ant CLI, Claude Code Analytics API. /ultrareview, auto mode for Max users. Desktop app GA. Fast mode for Opus 4.8 at 2x standard rate for 2.5x speed. June 15, 2026: Agent SDK / claude -p / GitHub Actions usage on subscription plans moves to a separate monthly credit ($20 Pro, $100 Max 5x, $200 Max 20x) billed at standard API rates; one-time opt-in claim required. Week 24 (June 8-16, 2026): nested sub-agents (background chains 5 deep, foreground unlimited), --safe-mode/CLAUDE_CODE_SAFE_MODE to isolate broken customizations, fallbackModel for up to 3 sequential model fallbacks, /cd mid-conversation working directory moves, auto mode on Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry for Opus 4.7/4.8, security-guidance plugin for real-time vulnerability reviews of Claude's code changes, --plugin list command, safer auto-edit prompts before writing risky files. Claude Code Artifacts launched in beta June 18, 2026 — Claude Code sessions turn into live, shareable HTML pages at private org-scoped URLs that update in place as work progresses (version history, gallery, auth-restricted to org members); rolling out to Claude Team and Enterprise customers via CLI and desktop app, powered by Opus 4.8. Claude Tag (Slack-native AI teammate) launched June 23, 2026 for Claude Enterprise / Team — persistent channel-scoped Claude instance with optional ambient mode for proactive follow-ups; single @Claude identity per org; 30-day migration from 'Claude in Slack' (powered by Claude Opus 4.8). Claude Code v2.1.190 (June 24, 2026) adds new 'seven_day_overage_included' rate limit category tracking Fable 5 weekly usage with specific 'You've reached your Fable 5 limit' message; model picker entry simplified to 'Requires usage credits'; model-scoped rate limits now returned in /status endpoint; Fable 5 still SUSPENDED globally pending Pentagon/NSA clearance on Fable 5 (Mythos 5 cleared June 26 for ~100 US orgs).

Microsoft.name: GitHub Copilot
Microsoft.description: Editor-native agent mode with GPT-5.5, Claude (Opus 4.8, Fable 5 — suspended June 12, 2026 by US export control directive), and Gemini model options. Agent mode for multi-file changes, documentation generation, PR review. Fable 5 was GA in Copilot (June 9, 2026) for Pro+/Max/Business/Enterprise requiring 30-day data retention. MAI-Thinking-1 in private preview on Foundry with GitHub Copilot integration.

Amazon.name: Kiro
Amazon.description: AI IDE with spec-driven development. Structured AI coding that turns specifications into implementations. Autonomous agent mode for background task completion.

JetBrains.name: JetBrains Junie
JetBrains.description: JetBrains AI coding agent — GA on June 17, 2026 (left beta). Advanced Plan mode (structured plan/requirements/design/delivery stages before coding), agentic debugging via the real debugger (not println), Remote Control (start task, monitor from phone, review PR over coffee), code review with full project context, deep IDE integration via ACP (Agent Communication Protocol) so Junie CLI talks to your IDE on the same protocol it uses with terminal clients. LLM-agnostic: works with Anthropic Claude Fable 5 (suspended), Opus 4.7, Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 3.1 Pro, GPT-5.5, Grok 4.3, plus local runtimes via LiteLLM/LMStudio/Ollama. BYOK supported; JetBrains AI Pro/Ultimate/Enterprise tiers with cloud credits and AI Credits top-up. SOC 2 certified. Mellum2 12B open-source model (June 1, 2026, Apache 2.0) — 2.5B active per token, <50% inference time vs comparable dense models, used as focal model for routing, summarization, and sub-agents. Rider 2026.2 EAP 5 (June 8, 2026) adds quality-check hooks for Claude Code and Codex (PostToolUse, runs IDE validation after agent edits). IntelliJ IDEA 2026.1.3 (June 4, 2026) brings tmux terminal fix and Markdown preview improvements.

Cursor.name: Cursor 3.8 (owned by SpaceX)
Cursor.description: AI-native editor (Cursor 3 unified workspace since April 2, 2026). Cursor 3.11 (July 10, 2026) — durable Side Chats via /side, /btw, or the plus button that branch off the running main agent for tangential questions without derailing the primary workflow; Conversation search via Cmd+K (local index scaling to thousands of transcripts) and Cmd+F within a single conversation; redesigned project and repo pickers scoped by location (This Computer, Cloud, Remote Machines) with multi-repo support and branch selection without leaving the picker; five new cloud-agent hook events (beforeSubmitPrompt, afterAgentResponse, afterAgentThought, stop, subagentStart) to inspect or gate agent reasoning on cloud VMs. Cursor 3.10 (June 30, 2026) — Customize page unifies Plugins/Skills/MCPs; Cursor for iOS in public beta on all paid plans (cloud agents on iPhone/iPad, Live Activities + push notifications, Remote Control handoff, generated artifact review, PR merge from phone, voice input, slash commands); 75% Composer 2.5 launch promo through July 5. Cursor 3.8 (June 18, 2026) Automations — /automate slash command to create automations from local agent sessions, 5 new GitHub triggers (issue comment, PR review comment/submitted, review thread updated, workflow run completed) and Slack emoji triggers; cloud agents now have computer use to produce demos/artifacts of work; templates for triaging failed GitHub Actions and auto-fixing PR review comments. Cursor 3.7 (June 4) Canvas Design Mode with multi-select and voice input, Context Usage Report, custom stores/tools, auto-review for SDK with subagent nesting. Enterprise Organizations framework GA (June 3, 2026) with three-layer governance (Org → Team → Group), centralized analytics, SCIM directory sync. Auto-review now default for new users (June 11, 2026, cursor.com/blog/agent-autonomy-auto-review). Bugbot 3x faster/22% cheaper/10% more bugs (June 10, ~90s review, in-house Composer 2.5 with model block list for fleet routing), now runnable with /review. Composer 2.5 default. cursor.com/agents cloud URL. Pro cut 40% to $12/mo on June 12, 2026 with new Efficiency Mode (up to 35% token reduction); enterprise spend controls and usage-based tiers above thresholds. Pro+ $60/mo, Ultra $200/mo. Gartner Leader. SpaceX announced all-stock $60B acquisition of Cursor on June 16, 2026 (after $1B+ ARR reached November 2025) — deal expected to close Q3 2026, gives SpaceX-xAI direct coding-tool arm to compete with Anthropic and OpenAI; existing termination fee of $1.5B + $8.5B in compute resources.

Cognition.name: Devin Desktop
Cognition.description: Cognition AI's agent-first IDE (formerly Windsurf, rebranded to Devin Desktop June 2, 2026, formal announcement June 7). Agent Command Center with Kanban view of local + cloud agents, Codemaps, one-click Devin cloud handoff, Spaces for project-level context. SWE-1.6 GA at 200 tok/s (Fireworks) / 950 tok/s (Cerebras). Devin Local 2026.5.26 in Rust, 30% more token-efficient than Cascade, subagent support, sandboxing. Cascade (Python) deprecated and removed July 1, 2026. Devin 2.2 (May 21, 2026): end-to-end testing with computer use, Review Autofix, 3x faster startup, redesigned interface. Devin Auto-Triage (May 18, 2026): Devin proactively responds to bug reports/incidents, investigates with connected tools, opens PRs. Agent Client Protocol (ACP) support for Codex, Claude Agent, OpenCode, and 25+ agents (JetBrains, Google, GitHub adoption). Agent router coming in weeks. June 19, 2026: MCP Marketplace Expansion adds 48+ engineering MCP connectors (Miro, Mixpanel, Honeycomb, Postman, monday.com, Klaviyo, LaunchDarkly with hosted OAuth, Fathom, Attio, Calendly, Google Drive GA for all); Devin Review for GitLab Merge Requests (intelligent diffs, inline comments, AI chat, sidebar by status); dedicated MCP Management Page for enterprise admins (per-server usage, per-session usage, org-wide rollups).

Microsoft-Code.name: MAI-Code-1-Flash
Microsoft-Code.description: Microsoft's inference-efficient coding model (June 2, 2026, Build) with 5B active parameters, 51% on SWE-Bench Pro, Haiku-class size but cheaper. Tuned for VS Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, and Microsoft stack. Rolling out as a default in VS Code for Copilot Free, Student, Pro, Pro+, and Max. First in a new wave of purpose-built coding models from Microsoft for GitHub Copilot.

Cohere.name: North Mini Code
Cohere.description: Cohere's first dedicated agentic coding model (launched June 15, 2026), 30B-parameter MoE with 3B active, Apache 2.0 from launch. Designed for multi-step, tool-using work in agents like Claude Code and Cursor. Brings Cohere's enterprise sovereignty framing to the developer layer — open weights give teams control over how coding agents evolve, optimize, and operate. Companion to the Command A+ enterprise family.

SpaceXAI.name: Grok Build
SpaceXAI.description: xAI coding agent and CLI (May 14, 2026) for SuperGrok/X Premium+ subscribers, in early beta. Plan mode for approve-before-execute workflows. Grok Build Plugin Marketplace (June 11, 2026) bundles skills, slash commands, agents, hooks, MCP servers, and LSPs into installable packages from MongoDB, Vercel, Sentry, Chrome DevTools, Cloudflare, Superpowers. /marketplace to browse. Parallel subagents, headless mode (-p) for scripting. ACP support for custom bots. June 15, 2026 update: multi-session manager — manage many coding sessions at once, see what each is doing, reply to ones that need you, dispatch new work. Composer 2.5 now default in /models menu (June 1, 2026). Grok Build 0.1 API ($1/$2 per 1M tokens, 100+ tok/s) public beta since May 29, 2026. Grok Build /goal command launched June 22, 2026 — long-running autonomous tasks with sub-agents implementing and verifying a single user-defined goal (significant repositioning of Grok Build as a multi-step agent platform). Firecrawl plugin (June 23, 2026) and MongoDB plugin (June 24, 2026) added to the Grok Build Plugin Marketplace. Grok + Interactive Brokers integration launched June 22, 2026 — query portfolio data, research investments, analyze positions using AI; trade execution requires explicit user approval.

Cursor-Router.name: Cursor Router
Cursor-Router.description: Cursor's intelligent model router (GA July 22, 2026 for Teams and Enterprise plans; on by default for Teams). Per-request classifier trained on 600k+ live requests, dispatches each prompt to the right model for the task. Three optimization modes: Intelligence (frontier quality, lands near Fable on satisfaction at ~60% lower cost), Balance (above Opus 4.8 at ~36% lower cost), and Cost (highest available intelligence while optimizing token spend). Reported cost per commit: $4.63 Balance, $6.76 Intelligence vs $7.34 Opus 4.8 and $12.69 Fable 5. Online A/B tests show frontier-quality output at 60% savings; three early-access enterprise accounts saved 30–50% vs Opus 4.8. Ships across desktop, web, iOS, CLI, and the Cursor SDK. Admin controls: per-team and per-group enablement, mode restrictions, default mode, model allow/block lists, soft and hard enforcement options for standardizing on Auto. Grok 4.5 is a required routing option (cannot be excluded). Balance and Intelligence bill at the routed model's rate; routed model is hidden by default and visible only when teams opt in.

OpenAI-Codex-Micro.name: Codex Micro
OpenAI-Codex-Micro.description: OpenAI's first hardware product (launched July 24, 2026, $230, sold via OpenAI Supply Co.) — a 13-key mechanical macropad / 'command center for agentic work' built in collaboration with Work Louder (rebranded Creator Micro 2). Bluetooth/USB-C, CNC-machined polycarbonate + aluminum body, PBT keycaps, clicky or silent switches, planar joystick, rotary encoder for adjusting Codex agent reasoning level. Pre-programmed macros for Codex Skills: open PRs, debug errors, refactor, review diffs. Sold out in under 24 hours. Ships amid an Apple lawsuit accusing OpenAI of stealing trade secrets for its Jony Ive-designed screen-free device.

Anthropic-Claude-Security.name: Claude Security Plugin
Anthropic-Claude-Security.description: Anthropic's multi-agent vulnerability scanner for Claude Code (released in beta July 22-23, 2026; current plugin v0.10.0). Runs a six-phase scan of a repository from inside an existing Claude Code session, then turns selected findings into patch files for review. Two entry points: /security-review for a one-time branch pass, or the Claude Security plugin for full-codebase deep scan with multi-agent review and patch generation. Three-voter adversarial panel (REACHABILITY/IMPACT/DEFENSES) must clear a 2-of-3 quorum before findings reach the report; non-unanimous votes cap stated confidence at medium. Patches built in an isolated scratch clone, independently verified, never auto-applied. Requires Claude Code v2.1.154+ with dynamic workflows enabled and Python 3.9.6+ / Git on PATH. Linux/macOS/Windows supported; counts against plan token limits.

SpaceXAI-Build-Mode.name: Grok Build Mode
SpaceXAI-Build-Mode.description: SpaceXAI's prompt-to-app builder inside Grok (launched July 28, 2026 in early beta; SuperGrok Heavy subscribers only at launch). Generates working websites, apps, games, and interactive dashboards from natural-language prompts; Grok writes the code, renders a live preview inside the chat, and accepts follow-up changes by chat. Once ready, projects publish to a grok.me address or a connected custom domain. Available on web, iOS, and Android. Ships 13 days after the open-source release of the Grok Build terminal coding agent (Rust source, MIT, July 15, 2026) — Build Mode wraps the same coding harness in a no-terminal consumer surface with managed hosting. Examples shown at launch include a physics playground and a browser-based beat machine.

BrowserStack.name: Test Companion
BrowserStack.description: BrowserStack's agentic AI for test automation inside the IDE (launched July 29, 2026, Dublin). Closes the gap between authored tests and existing code/frameworks/testing stack with no setup or context switching. Accelerates test authoring, execution, debugging, and maintenance across web and mobile apps; teams report 4x faster test authoring, debugging, and maintenance. Newest addition to BrowserStack AI portfolio (2025: 20+ agents across the testing lifecycle; open-source BrowserStack MCP Server connects the testing platform to GitHub Copilot, Cursor, and Claude). 1,000+ teams already use Test Companion; installs from the marketplace in VS Code, JetBrains, Cursor, and Antigravity.

Google.name: Gemini CLI
Google.description: Open terminal agent linked to Gemini Code Assist and Gemini model workflows. MCP protocol support.

OpenAI.name: Codex CLI
OpenAI.description: Terminal coding agent powered by GPT-5.5 and Codex. Cloud and local execution modes. Available on macOS (Windows host connection coming). Remote control from ChatGPT mobile (May 14, 2026).

Anthropic.name: Claude Code
Anthropic.description: Terminal-first coding agent with IDE workflows powered by Claude Opus 4.8 (Claude Fable 5 SUSPENDED June 12–June 30, 2026 by US export control directive — REDEPLOYED July 1, 2026 after US export controls lifted (new safety classifier blocks the Amazon-reported technique in 99%+ cases) — was available via API). Dynamic workflows now GA (May 28, 2026 research preview → June 11, 2026 GA, Code with Claude Tokyo) for parallel sub-agents at scale. /ultracode or ask Claude to create a workflow. Scheduled deployments and env var vaults in public beta for Claude Managed Agents (June 11, 2026). ant CLI, Analytics API. /ultrareview, auto mode for Max users. Desktop app GA. v2.1.173 (June 11, 2026) normalizes Fable 5 model names with [1m] suffix. June 15, 2026: claude -p (headless) and Agent SDK calls move to a separate monthly credit pool per user ($20 Pro, $100 Max 5x, $200 Max 20x), no rollover, one-time opt-in claim. Week 24 (June 8-16, 2026): nested sub-agents that can spawn their own agents (background chains capped 5 deep, foreground unlimited), --safe-mode / CLAUDE_CODE_SAFE_MODE to launch with all customizations disabled, fallbackModel for up to 3 sequential model fallbacks, /cd session moves (change working directory mid-conversation without breaking prompt cache), localized session titles, --plugin list command, managed deployment version controls, security-guidance plugin for real-time vulnerability reviews of Claude's code changes, auto mode on Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry for Opus 4.7/4.8, safer auto-edit prompts before writing risky files. Sub-agent panel below prompt shows full tree with descendant counts and path back to main. Claude Tag (Slack-native AI teammate) launched June 23, 2026 for Claude Enterprise / Team — persistent channel-scoped Claude instance with optional ambient mode for proactive follow-ups; single @Claude identity per org; 30-day migration from 'Claude in Slack' (powered by Claude Opus 4.8).

JetBrains.name: TeamCity CLI
JetBrains.description: Free, lightweight open-source CLI for TeamCity CI/CD. Enables AI agents to check build status, analyze failures, interact with Pipeline. MCP support for third-party AI tooling (May 12, 2026).

Courier.name: Courier CLI
Courier.description: Q2 2026 CLI for giving AI agents notification infrastructure and JSON-safe commands.

Amazon.name: Amazon Q CLI
Amazon.description: Command-line assistant for AWS operations, code changes, and shell workflows.

HuggingFace.name: Hugging Face CLI
HuggingFace.description: The new `hf` CLI (rebuilt June 4, 2026) is the official command-line entrypoint to the Hugging Face Hub, now agent-optimized. Detects when a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, Pi) is driving it via CLAUDECODE/CODEX_SANDBOX/AI_AGENT env vars and switches to agent-mode output (no ANSI, full values, structured) for up to 6x fewer tokens. Manage models/datasets/Spaces, create repos/branches/PRs, run Jobs, manage Buckets/Collections/webhooks/Inference Endpoints. huggingface_hub v1.15.0 (May 15, 2026) adds region-aware buckets and repos, `hf skills list`, polished CLI help.

Mistral.name: Mistral Vibe
Mistral.description: Open-source terminal-native coding agent powered by Mistral Medium 3.5. Remote cloud sandboxes via Vibe Code Workflow (May 5, 2026), parallel async sessions, GitHub PR integration. Le Chat rebranded to Vibe (May 28, 2026) — Work Mode and Code Mode under one agent and one license, all Le Chat history preserved. Vibe remote agents (May 22, 2026) can teleport local sessions to cloud when work outgrows laptop. Connectors in Studio with custom MCPs (May 22, 2026). New VS Code extension and JetBrains/Zed ACP integration. Code Mode adds remote sessions from Vibe web surface with GitHub integration and Slack triggers (June). Mistral Medium 3.5 also on Microsoft Copilot Studio (May 28, 2026) with EU data residency. Vibe 2.0 terminal release June 18, 2026 — adds custom subagents, multi-choice clarifications, slash-command skills; Devstral 2 API pricing now $0.40/M input and $2.00/M output tokens (smaller variant $0.10/$0.30).

Zapier.name: Zapier Platform CLI
Zapier.description: CLI for building AI-enabled integrations, actions, and MCP-style tooling.

n8n.name: n8n CLI
n8n.description: CLI for workflow lifecycle, self-hosting, and automation operations.

NVIDIA.name: AI Workbench CLI
NVIDIA.description: CLI-backed local and remote AI dev environments for model teams.

Cognition.name: Devin CLI
Cognition.description: Cognition AI's local coding agent CLI (June 4, 2026) — run Devin right in your shell, with local/remote execution across Opus 4.7, GPT-5.5, and SWE-1.6. Custom terminal rendering in Rust for fast, snappy UI. Hand off long-running sessions to cloud agents with their own sandboxed computers when local isn't enough; resume in CLI or open PR. Install: `curl -fsSL https://cli.devin.ai/install.sh | bash`. ACP support for Codex, Claude Agent, OpenCode.

SpaceXAI.name: Grok Build CLI
SpaceXAI.description: xAI terminal coding agent (May 14, 2026) for SuperGrok/X Premium+ subscribers, in early beta. Plan mode, parallel subagents, deep worktree integrations. Grok Build Plugin Marketplace (June 11, 2026) for installing skills/MCP/plugins from MongoDB, Vercel, Sentry, Chrome DevTools, Cloudflare, Superpowers. ACP support for custom bots and orchestration. Headless mode for CI/CD. grok-build-0.1 API (May 29, 2026) at $1/$2 per 1M tokens, 100+ tok/s. June 15, 2026 update: multi-session manager — manage many coding sessions at once, see what each is doing, reply to ones that need you, dispatch new work. Composer 2.5 now default in /models menu (June 1, 2026). Grok V9-Medium (1.5T params, Cursor-trained coding model) finished training May 25 with public release expected mid-June 2026. Grok for Word add-in launched June 18, 2026 — free Microsoft 365 add-in for Word (and PowerPoint/Excel) brings Grok-powered drafting, research, and rewriting into Office documents via connectors (SharePoint, Google Drive). Grok Build /goal command launched June 22, 2026 — long-running autonomous tasks with sub-agents implementing and verifying a single user-defined goal (significant repositioning of Grok Build as a multi-step agent platform). Firecrawl plugin (June 23, 2026) and MongoDB plugin (June 24, 2026) added to the Grok Build Plugin Marketplace. Grok + Interactive Brokers integration launched June 22, 2026 — query portfolio data, research investments, analyze positions using AI; trade execution requires explicit user approval.

Google.name: Gemini API
Google.description: Developer platform for Gemini models, tools, embeddings, and multimodal apps. File Search now multimodal (May 5). Higher-res images, custom metadata. Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS in preview. Gemini 3.5 Live Translate audio model in public preview via Gemini Live API (June 9, 2026). Managed Agents API for autonomous agentic workflows (May 2026).
